page: Amazon Web Services x8g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by the AWS Nitro System and 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs built on the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The cache topology includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per socket or domain. It is provisioned with 3,072.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 16.0 GB per-core allocation. Networking provides a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU performance scored 314,681.65 (top 10%), while single-core performance registered 1,644.19 (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests reflect substantial throughput, measuring 895.67 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 408.32 GB/sec for large write blocks. Database and caching benchmarks highlight extreme scalability, recording 359.81 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and top-tier PassMark database performance (46,223.77). Compiling with Clang (87,427.0) and ray tracing (150,650.0) also landed in the top tier.

The 16:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers distinct resource density advantages for architectures constrained by memory footprint rather than single-threaded raw speed. While single-thread execution is average, the massive aggregate memory capacity coupled with 192 dedicated physical cores maximizes cost efficiency for parallelized, memory-dense workloads. The primary operational tradeoff is the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage IOPS must be provisioned via network-attached volumes.

Given its massive memory scale and high multi-threaded performance, the x8g.48xlarge is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, large-scale enterprise databases, heavy multi-threaded compile tasks, and big data in-memory processing frameworks.
